Surat al-Jumu'ah

This surah was named by the Companions and in the books of Sunnah and tafsir "Surat al-Jumu'ah" (the Surah of Friday), and no other name for it is known. In Sahih al-Bukhari, from Abu Hurayra, who said, "We were sitting with the Prophet when Surat al-Jumu'ah was revealed to him," and the hadith continues. Its explanation will come at the commentary on His words, ﴿and others among them who have not yet joined them﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 3].

The reason for its name is the occurrence in it of the word *al-Jumu'ah*, which is the name for the seventh day of the week in Islam.

Tha'lab said that the Quraysh used to gather on it at Qusayy's House of Assembly (*Dar al-Nadwa*). But this does not imply that they named that day "al-Jumu'ah."

I have not found in the speech of the Arabs before Islam anything establishing that they applied the name al-Jumu'ah to this day.

The name *al-Jumu'ah* has been applied to the prayer prescribed on it, by omitting the annexed term for frequency of use. In the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, 'When one of you comes to the Jumu'ah, let him perform ghusl,'" and in the speech of 'A'isha there occurs, "The people used to come to the Jumu'ah from their homes and from al-'Awali," etc.

In the words of Anas, "We used to take a midday nap after the Jumu'ah," and from the words of Ibn 'Umar, "The Messenger of God did not pray after the Jumu'ah until he left," meaning from the mosque. And from the words of

[Page 205]

Sahl ibn Sa'd: "We did not take a midday nap or have lunch except after the Jumu'ah." So it is possible that the word "Jumu'ah" in the name of this surah means the Friday prayer, because this surah contains rulings on the Friday prayer. It is also possible that it means the day of Friday, because the phrase "the day of Friday" occurs in the surah in the verse about the Friday prayer.

It is Medinan by consensus.

It appears that it was revealed in the sixth year AH, which is the year of Khaybar. The apparent meaning of the hadith of Abu Hurayra that we mentioned just above is that this surah was revealed after the conquest of Khaybar, because Abu Hurayra embraced Islam on the day of Khaybar.

Its apparent meaning is that it was revealed all at once, so the matter of the caravan's arrival from Syria would be the cause of the revelation of the surah, and this will be mentioned later.

Commentary of Ibn 'Ashur (al-Tahrir wa al-Tanwir) on surah 61, verse 14 (part 2 of 2):

The obligation of the Friday prayer (salat al-Jumu'ah) had already been established before the revelation of this surah. The Prophet (ﷺ) made it obligatory in a sermon (khutbah) he delivered to the people, and he led the prayer on the first Friday after the Hijra (the migration to Madina) in the house of the Banu Salim ibn 'Awf. It is established that the people of Madina performed it before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in Madina, as will come. Its obligation was therefore established by the sunnah (the normative practice of the Prophet), both in his words and in his actions. What is mentioned in this surah, his saying ﴿When the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then hasten to the remembrance of Allah﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 9], came as an emphasis on attending the Friday prayer and abandoning trade, and as a warning against leaving during the prayer before it is completed, as will come.

This surah is counted as the one hundred and sixth in the order of revelation of the surahs according to Jabir ibn Zayd. It was revealed after Surah al-Tahrim and before Surah al-Taghabun.

The apparent meaning of the hadith of Abu Hurayra indicates that this surah was revealed all at once, not in installments.

Its verses are counted as eleven, by the agreement of the reckoners (al-'Addin) among the readers of the major cities (qurra' al-amsar).

* * *

The first of its purposes, the reason for which it was revealed, is the warning against neglecting the Friday prayer,

Page 206

and the command to abandon whatever distracts from it during the time of its performance. To prepare for this, the surah first highlights the majesty of Allah, the Exalted, and honors the Messenger (ﷺ), that he is a messenger to the Arabs and to those who will join them.

And that his mission to them is a bounty from Allah.

In this there is a preparation for censuring the Jews, because they envied the Muslims for being honored with this religion.

Among what they envied and resented them for was that the day of Friday was made the most excellent day of the week, after it had been the day of Saturday, which was well known in those lands.

Also, the refutation of their claim that they are the friends of Allah.

And the rebuke of a people who turned away from it (the prayer) because of the arrival of a trade caravan from Syria.
